$comment: Feed this file to Gemini / Nano Banana Pro to generate the RideIQ architecture diagram. Use the 'image_prompt' as the main instruction and the 'spec' below as the exact structure to draw. Folder named 'Diagram' (your note said 'Dairgam').

meta.subtitle: Ride-hailing brain — Android app + FastAPI ML backend, deployed to AWS EC2 with blue-green CI/CD

image_prompt: Create a clean, professional software architecture diagram, left-to-right flow, flat modern style with soft rounded rectangles, subtle drop shadows, and clear labeled arrows. Show four vertical zones separated by faint dashed boundaries: (1) CLIENT — an Android phone running the RideIQ app with two screens (Quote screen, OpenStreetMap route screen). (2) CI/CD PIPELINE — GitHub push on main triggering a GitHub Actions cloud runner that builds a Docker image and pushes it to the ghcr.io container registry, then SSHes into the server to run a blue-green swap. (3) AWS EC2 HOST — a box (the VM) containing an nginx edge reverse-proxy on port 80, two app containers labeled 'rideiq-blue' and 'rideiq-green' where only one is live at a time (draw green as ACTIVE/solid, blue as IDLE/faded), a shared Redis cache container, a SQLite database on a mounted volume, and a baked-in city_graph.json (Edmonton road network). (4) ML BRAIN inside the live app container — a stack of 8 feature boxes: ETA prediction, Fare estimation, Cancellation risk, Fraud check, Surge zones, Rider segments, Driver shift, Cancellation causes, plus an A* routing engine. Draw the request path as a bold arrow: phone → Elastic Public IP → nginx :80 → live color :8000 → ML brain. Draw the deploy path as a separate colored arrow: GitHub Actions → ghcr.io and GitHub Actions → SSH → nginx swap. Add a small 'rollback' loop arrow from a stored old image back into the swap. Use a legend explaining ACTIVE vs IDLE color and the two arrow types (traffic vs deploy). Keep text crisp and readable; label every arrow with its protocol (HTTP, SSH, Docker pull, Redis, SQLite).

style.shapes: rounded rectangles for services, cylinder for databases, phone frame for client, dashed box for the EC2 host boundary

legend.means: IDLE color (previous version, kept for rollback)

nodes.label: GitHub Actions
nodes.sublabel: on push to main / manual rollback

nodes.label: city_graph.json
nodes.sublabel: Edmonton OSM road network, baked into image

annotations: Only ONE color (blue/green) serves traffic at a time; the other is kept for instant rollback.
New color must pass /health before nginx is repointed -> zero-downtime deploys.
Rollback = re-run the workflow with an old commit SHA; build is skipped, old image redeployed.
Redis + SQLite volume + city_graph.json are the three stateful/asset pieces that must persist across swaps.
